title: Present & Past Tenses
objective: Choose correctly between present simple/continuous, past simple/continuous and present perfect at B1 level.

sections.heading: Present Simple vs Present Continuous
sections.body:
Use the **Present Simple** for facts, habits and timetables: `She works in a bank.` `The train leaves at 9.15.`
Use the **Present Continuous** for actions happening now or around now, and fixed future arrangements: `I'm studying for my exam this week.` `We're flying to Rome on Friday.`
sections.bodyZh: 一般现在时用于事实、习惯和时刻表；现在进行时用于此刻或近期正在发生的事，以及已安排好的将来计划。

examples.en: My sister usually walks to school, but today she is taking the bus.
examples.zh: 我妹妹通常走路去上学，但今天她坐公交车。

examples.en: What are you doing this evening? I'm meeting some friends.
examples.zh: 你今晚做什么？我要和几个朋友见面。

sections.tip: Stative verbs (know, like, believe, understand, want) almost never take the continuous form. Say `I know`, not `I am knowing`.

sections.heading: Past Simple vs Past Continuous
sections.body:
Use the **Past Simple** for finished actions at a known time: `We arrived at six.`
Use the **Past Continuous** for a background action in progress when something else happened: `While I was waiting for the bus, it started to rain.`
sections.bodyZh: 一般过去时用于在明确时间完成的动作；过去进行时用于另一件事发生时正在进行的背景动作。

examples.en: She was reading a book when the phone rang.
We didn't go out because it was raining.
examples.zh: 我们没出门，因为当时正在下雨。

sections.tip: In exam stories, the classic pattern is: Past Continuous (background) + when + Past Simple (sudden event).

sections.heading: Present Perfect
sections.body:
Use the **Present Perfect** (`have/has + past participle`) for life experience, recent events with present results, and unfinished time periods. Typical signals: `ever, never, just, already, yet, since, for`.
`I have never been to Japan.` `She has just finished her homework.` `We have lived here since 2019.`
sections.bodyZh: 现在完成时（have/has + 过去分词）用于人生经历、对现在有影响的近期事件和尚未结束的时间段。常见信号词：ever、never、just、already、yet、since、for。

examples.en: Have you ever eaten sushi? — Yes, I've tried it twice.
examples.zh: 你吃过寿司吗？——吃过，我试过两次。

examples.en: I can't pay for the coffee. I've lost my wallet!
examples.zh: 我付不了咖啡钱。我把钱包弄丢了！

sections.tip: Never use the Present Perfect with a finished past time word. `I have seen him yesterday` is wrong — say `I saw him yesterday`.

commonErrors.why: 'know' is a stative verb; it is not used in the continuous form.

commonErrors.wrong: I have seen that film last week.
commonErrors.right: I saw that film last week.
commonErrors.why: 'last week' is a finished time — use Past Simple.

commonErrors.wrong: When I was arriving, he left.
commonErrors.why: Two short completed actions both take Past Simple.

keyPoints: Present Continuous = now / around now / future arrangements.
Past Continuous sets the scene; Past Simple is the event.
Present Perfect connects past and present — never with finished time words.
